acceptance_criteria.criterion: All mandated directories exist and are registered in the workspace; workspace installation succeeds from the committed lockfile.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: packages/{core,world,domain,application,narrative,contracts,adapters,ui}, apps/desktop/{main,preload,renderer,simulation-worker}, tools/{replay,bench,package}, and docs/decisions all created. pnpm-workspace.yaml registers packages/*, apps/desktop/*, and tools/*. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` reports 'Lockfile is up to date' and completes with all 16 workspace projects installed. Verified by tests/config/workspace.test.mjs.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every TypeScript project inherits strict:true and noUncheckedIndexedAccess:true, and the root compile command exits successfully.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: tsconfig.base.json sets both flags; every per-project tsconfig extends it and adds nothing that overrides them. tests/config/tsconfig.test.mjs enumerates the 15 mandated TS projects and asserts inherited strict/noUncheckedIndexedAccess resolve to true, plus verifies tsconfig.json project-references cover all 15. `pnpm run compile` (tsc -b) exits 0.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The lint configuration treats all packages as pure by default and limits impurity exceptions to the packages explicitly permitted by the specification.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: eslint.config.mjs applies PURE_RULES to the glob packages/**/*.ts and only IMPURE_OVERRIDE_RULES ({no-console/no-restricted-globals/no-restricted-imports/no-restricted-syntax → off}) to packages/adapters/** and packages/ui/**. Newly added packages automatically inherit the pure rules. tests/config/workspace.test.mjs asserts pure-by-default and that the impure allowlist is exactly ['adapters','ui']. Ad-hoc probe confirmed Math.random errors under packages/core but not packages/adapters.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The blocking lint command rejects representative uses of Math.random, wall-clock APIs, prohibited transcendental Math functions, fetch, console, nondeterministic collection traversal, comparator-free Array.sort, forbidden JSON serialization of economic structures, and Node/Electron imports from pure packages.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: tests/fixtures/lint/forbidden contains one .ts fixture per prohibition (math-random, wall-clock-date-now, wall-clock-set-timeout, wall-clock-performance, transcendental, fetch, console, nondeterministic-object-keys, nondeterministic-for-in, array-sort-no-comparator, json-stringify-economic, node-import, electron-import). tests/lint/rules.test.mjs runs the ESLint programmatic API with PURE_RULES and asserts each fixture triggers the expected rule id and message keyword; all 13 assertions pass. `pnpm run lint --max-warnings=0` exits 0 on the committed working tree.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The dependency-boundary command rejects imports outside the Section 14.5 directed graph and exits successfully for the repository's valid imports.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: tools/boundary/lib.mjs encodes the exact Section 14.5 DIRECT_EDGES map and computes its transitive closure; tools/boundary/check.mjs walks every workspace src/ tree, extracts import specifiers, and rejects any @ciclo/* edge outside the closure. `pnpm run boundary` prints 'dependency-boundary: OK. 15 workspace packages validated against Section 14.5.' and exits 0. tests/boundary/graph.test.mjs verifies 15 allowed edges, 15 representative forbidden direct edges, transitive reach apps→core, a transitive violation on a mock linear graph, and a CLI end-to-end run against a synthetic workspace with a forbidden packages/core → @ciclo/domain import that exits 1 with 'Forbidden edge core -> domain'.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: CI runs clean installation, compilation, lint, dependency-boundary validation, and tests; every job passes on the committed repository state.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs on push and pull_request. Steps: checkout → setup-node using .nvmrc → pnpm/action-setup@v4 pinned to 9.15.0 → pnpm install --frozen-lockfile → pnpm run compile → pnpm run lint → pnpm run boundary → pnpm run test. All five commands were executed locally on the committed tree and each exited 0; the four gate scripts are the same commands the workflow calls.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: SPEC_BLOCKERS.md exists and provides the Section 19 fields without inventing or resolving a specification contradiction.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: /workspace/SPEC_BLOCKERS.md describes the Section 19 protocol, provides an entry template with the required fields (identifier, sections in conflict, impact, affected work fronts, status, and provisional-decision fields), and keeps the Open/Provisional/Resolved sections empty. No blocker or provisional decision is fabricated.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No production algorithm or unresolved DEFINIR-dependent behavior is introduced.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Every packages/*/src/index.ts, apps/desktop/*/src/index.ts, and tools/*/src/index.ts contains only `export {};`. docs/decisions holds only a README explaining the ADR process; no ADR is authored. No numeric parameters, hash function, rounding mode, encoding definition, IMPACT_WINDOW, BOT_DECISION_PERIOD, octave count, or ruleset semantic is committed.

discovered_out_of_scope_issues: CICLO_SPEC §14.5 codifies edges for packages, apps, and (implicitly) core; it does not list edges for tools/*. This is not a contradiction — §14.4 places tools outside packages/, §13 flags them as impure by nature — but the FASE-1 tools/replay and tools/bench acceptance items in §15 will require an ADR or spec blocker that names their allowed edges before their production behavior can be delivered.
known_issues: When tools/replay and tools/bench eventually need to import @ciclo/application (per FASE-1 acceptance items 'tools/replay compares two runs' and 'tools/bench calibration'), the Section 14.5 graph — which only names apps → adapters, ui, contracts — will need an explicit tools edge set. The FASE-1 bootstrap deliberately leaves tools with no cross-workspace imports so the graph is enforced verbatim; the future ADR (or spec blocker under Section 19) resolves the extension. No production behavior of replay/bench is delivered by this task.
notes_for_reviewer: The lint 'pure by negation' semantics is enforced by two flat-config blocks: packages/**/*.ts gets PURE_RULES, then packages/adapters/**/*.ts and packages/ui/**/*.ts turn the four deterministic-rule ids off. A new package added under packages/ automatically inherits the pure rules with no config change, satisfying the 'cannot pass by silently excluding newly added package source files' must-preserve.

The lint fixtures live under tests/fixtures/** which is in the ESLint ignore list, so the main `pnpm run lint` stays clean. tests/lint/rules.test.mjs re-lints each fixture programmatically with `overrideConfigFile: true` and PURE_RULES only, and asserts on both rule id and a message keyword, so a rule renamed or relaxed still fails the test.

tools/boundary/check.mjs uses process.env.CICLO_REPO_ROOT ?? process.cwd() so a test can point the CLI at a synthetic workspace; the boundary test exercises that path end-to-end to confirm the tool exits 1 (not just that lib.mjs reports violations).

Every package.json manifest declares only workspace edges that are permitted by Section 14.5 (e.g., apps/desktop/simulation-worker depends on adapters+contracts, not application/domain directly). If the reviewer expects direct edges from simulation-worker into application/domain, that would need a Section 14.5 amendment ADR — the current strict reading of the graph does not allow apps to import application directly, only transitively through adapters.
payload.summary: Bootstrapped the CICLO pnpm workspace. Created the eight mandated packages (core, world, domain, application, narrative, contracts, adapters, ui), the four desktop apps (main, preload, renderer, simulation-worker), the three tools (replay, bench, package), and docs/decisions, each with a package manifest and, for TS projects, a tsconfig extending a strict base (strict:true and noUncheckedIndexedAccess:true), with a root project-references tsconfig. Installed dependencies from a committed pnpm lockfile. Wired an ESLint 9 flat config that treats packages/** as pure by default (via glob) and only relaxes the deterministic-code rules for the specification-authorized adapters/ui allowlist. The pure ruleset blocks Math.random, wall-clock APIs (Date, Date.now, performance.now, setTimeout/setInterval), transcendental Math (sin/cos/tan/exp/log/pow/sqrt/…), fetch/XMLHttpRequest/WebSocket, crypto.randomUUID/randomBytes/getRandomValues, toLocaleString/Intl, Object.keys/values/entries/for-in traversal, comparator-free Array.sort, JSON.stringify/parse, and imports of Electron, node:* built-ins, database drivers, and network/filesystem clients. Implemented tools/boundary/check.mjs that walks every workspace TS source file, extracts static and dynamic import specifiers, and validates them (including transitively) against the Section 14.5 directed graph. Added executable rule tests: one failing fixture per Section 13 category and a clean authorized fixture (verified via the ESLint programmatic API), Section 14.5 graph unit tests covering every allowed edge, representative forbidden edges (including a transitive violation via a mock graph), and a CLI end-to-end test that runs the boundary tool against a synthetic workspace with a forbidden core→domain edge. Added a configuration test enumerating every mandated TypeScript project and verifying inherited strict/noUncheckedIndexedAccess. Added a GitHub Actions CI job that runs pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, compile, lint, boundary, and test on every push and pull request. Created SPEC_BLOCKERS.md with the Section 19 fields and an empty registry (no contradiction invented or resolved). No production algorithm, DEFINIR resolution, or economic parameter was introduced — every package source file is a placeholder export {}.

validation.summary: Lockfile up to date; 16 workspace projects installed without resolution.
tsc -b succeeds for all 15 TypeScript project references.
eslint . --max-warnings=0 exits 0 on the committed working tree.
tools/boundary/check.mjs validates all 15 workspace packages against Section 14.5 with no violations.
28/28 tests pass across tests/config, tests/lint, and tests/boundary (structure, tsconfig, pure-lint fixtures, and dependency graph).
